report.source_text: On examination, the patient was afebrile and normotensive, with an oxygen saturation of 96% on room air. There was pronounced oedema involving the lingual mucosa and subcutaneous tissues of the perioral area without pain or pruritus. Cardiac auscultation revealed tachycardia without any pathological murmurs. Auscultation of the lungs revealed decreased breath sounds bilaterally with inspiratory effort, but no wheezing or crepitations. No jugular venous distention or lower limb swelling was appreciated. No urticarial eruption was noted throughout.

clinician.final_diagnosis: ACE inhibitor-induced angioedema with concomitant COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old man on benazepril for 4 months presented with worsening tongue swelling, difficulty speaking, and shortness of breath. Physical examination revealed pronounced lingual and perioral edema, tachycardia, and decreased breath sounds bilaterally. There was no urticaria, pain, or pruritus. Initial management included withholding benazepril, and administering tranexamic acid, diphenhydramine, and famotidine, leading to clinical improvement of the angioedema within 3 hours. He was admitted for airway monitoring. A chest X-ray showed bilateral infiltrates in lung bases, and a SARS-CoV-2 PCR test later returned positive, confirming a concomitant COVID-19 infection.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient was taking benazepril, an ACE inhibitor, for approximately 4 months prior to presentation.
Patient presented with worsening swelling of the tongue, difficulty in speaking, and shortness of breath.
Physical examination revealed pronounced oedema involving the lingual mucosa and subcutaneous tissues of the perioral area.
No pain, pruritus, or urticarial eruption was noted, consistent with bradykinin-mediated angioedema.
Benazepril was withheld, and the patient's clinical presentation improved over 3 hours after administration of tranexamic acid.
A SARS-CoV-2 PCR test returned positive.
Chest X-ray showed bilateral infiltrates in lung bases.
Auscultation of the lungs revealed decreased breath sounds bilaterally with inspiratory effort.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Absence of pain, pruritus, or urticarial eruption (E001). Patient denied allergies or eating anything outside his regular diet (initial_presentation).

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Hereditary or acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency angioedema
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Patient had no personal or family history of facial or tongue swelling (initial_presentation), suggesting an acquired cause related to medication.
